title: The Vector of Station Meridian
premise: Jonah Yarrow has spent eleven years alone on Station Meridian, tending Earth's abandoned seed vault and broadcasting maintenance logs to a colony fleet that stopped answering years ago. When gravity flickers for nine seconds across the entire system, she discovers the flicker was a weapon test — and that the two fleets converging on Meridian, the loyalist Remnant and the breakaway Concord, each believe the other fired it. A corrupted transmission from the vault's old command AI gives Jonah proof of who really did, but revealing it will shatter the fragile truce that keeps both fleets from destroying the station and its seeds. To buy time, Jonah fabricates a counter-lie: she claims Meridian's archives hold a doomsday failsafe keyed to her biometrics. The deception holds the fleets apart long enough for her to smuggle the true evidence to a defector courier, but at the cost of her own standing — in the end, both fleets depart believing her a traitor, while the seeds and the truth leave Meridian together, and Jonah stays behind with only her logs and, at last, an honest record.
about_author: Ada Vane is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete agricultural data before turning to fiction full-time. She writes quiet, claustrophobic science fiction about people left behind by grand narratives.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: POV Jonah Yarrow. Establishes Jonah's solitary routine aboard Station Meridian: tending seed vaults, recording logs for a colony fleet that no longer replies. Mid-chapter, gravity across the entire system stutters for exactly nine seconds; Jonah floats, terrified and exhilarated, as her greenhouse floods and her instruments scream. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by sudden, impossible contact with a universe that noticed her.

chapters.title: The Log Nobody Reads
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. In the aftermath, Jonah repairs the station and replays sensor data: the flicker originated not from any fleet but from deep space near the derelict relay Kestrel-7. She drafts her first honest log entry in years — then hesitates, realizing whoever caused this may be listening. Emotional beat: the habit of performing normalcy warring with the need to tell the truth.

chapters.title: Two Flags on the Horizon
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Long-range scopes reveal two fleets inbound: the Remnant, flying the old colonial charter, and the breakaway Concord, both claiming Meridian as neutral ground for talks. Neither answers her hails. Jonah realizes the nine-second event is why they've come — and that both sides think the other did it. Emotional beat: dread of becoming a stage for someone else's war.

chapters.title: Docking Protocols
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The Remnant corvette Vespera docks first; its captain, Ilsa Rehn, treats Jonah with careful courtesy that reads as suspicion. Jonah gives the tour, hiding the vault's deepest archive behind a sealed bulkhead. A Concord shuttle shadows the docking bay, uninvited. Emotional beat: the strange vertigo of being perceived after years alone.

chapters.title: What the Seeds Remember
chapters.summary: POV Jonah, with intercut excerpts of the vault AI Meridian-Core's degraded logs. Rehn asks about the nine seconds; Jonah shares raw telemetry honestly — and watches Rehn's aide quietly alter the file before transmitting it to the fleet. Jonah understands evidence here is already fiction. Emotional beat: first betrayal, delivered politely.

chapters.title: The Concord Envoy
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Concord envoy Dae-Sun Okoro arrives under flag of parley and, over contraband tea, tells Jonah a different story: the Remnant tested a gravity weapon at Kestrel-7 and blamed them preemptively. His grief seems genuine. Jonah recognizes she is being recruited by both sides. Emotional beat: sympathy as a weapon aimed at her.

chapters.title: Kestrel-7
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Using the station's ancient tug, Jonah makes a risky solo run to the derelict relay and finds scorch patterns consistent with neither fleet's drive signatures — a third party. She recovers a black box fragment before a patrol scares her off. Emotional beat: the thrill of independent discovery curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Meridian-Core Wakes
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Back home, Jonah feeds the black box to the vault AI, which partially reboots and reveals it recorded the nine seconds in full: the signature belongs to a private armature company thought dissolved — Halcyon Dynamics, once contracted by both fleets. The AI warns its own memory banks were tampered with years ago. Emotional beat: hope that truth exists somewhere intact.

chapters.title: The Truce Table
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Both fleets' delegations meet in Meridian's hydroponics chapel to negotiate. Jonah, as neutral host, watches each side present doctored versions of her own telemetry. When she almost speaks, Rehn's aide catches her eye and shakes his head — a warning. Emotional beat: complicity by silence, and how much it costs.

chapters.title: A Lie With Good Posture
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. That night, Jonah invents the failsafe: she broadcasts that Meridian's archives contain a dead-man's-switch keyed to her biometrics, armed if the station is seized. It's fabricated — but plausible enough that both fleets stand down their boarding parties. Emotional beat: the intoxicating, shameful power of a well-told lie.

chapters.title: Okoro's Doubt
chapters.summary: POV Dae-Sun Okoro (first non-Jonah POV). Okoro suspects the failsafe is false but also suspects his own command is lying about Kestrel-7. He confronts Jonah privately; she neither confirms nor denies, and he chooses to protect her lie because he needs it to be true. Emotional beat: two liars granting each other mercy.

chapters.title: Tampering
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Someone breaks into the vault's lower archive overnight. Meridian-Core identifies the intruder's gait as Rehn's aide, Pell. Jonah finds her original telemetry deleted and a forged weapons-test file planted in its place. Emotional beat: violation — her home rewritten without her consent.

chapters.title: The Courier Question
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah needs the surviving black-box copy off-station before Pell's forgery becomes fleet doctrine. The only candidate is Juno Park, a Remnant defector pilot grounded for insubordination, who hates both commands equally. Jonah tests her loyalty with a half-truth. Emotional beat: learning to trust strategically rather than warmly.

chapters.title: Countdown Etiquette
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Fleet negotiators set a deadline: unresolved custody of Meridian in six days means joint occupation — meaning war by attrition. Jonah's failsafe bluff buys days, not peace, and both sides begin probing it with escalating provocations. Emotional beat: time as a tightening band around her chest.

chapters.title: Pell's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Pell corners Jonah and reveals he works for Halcyon remnants embedded in the Remnant command; he offers her wealth and passage in exchange for the black box and silence. He also confirms the nine seconds were a market manipulation — engineered scarcity to force the fleets into a merger Halcyon would broker. Emotional beat: disgust at how cheap the truth's price is.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah declines and prepares Juno's escape run, but Meridian-Core flags a problem: transmitting the evidence requires opening the deep archive, which will expose the failsafe as fiction. Jonah must choose between the truth's survival and the lie holding the fleets apart. Emotional beat: the moment loyalty to people outranks loyalty to safety.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: POV Juno Park. Juno launches with the black box hidden in her drive plume, threading between both fleets' picket lines while Jonah runs interference from the station, feeding false targeting solutions. Juno takes fire, loses comms, and goes dark past the belt. Emotional beat: terror and fierce, unexpected solidarity.

chapters.title: Exposure
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Pell exposes the failsafe as fabrication, having decrypted Jonah's fake biometric key. Both fleets demand her surrender; Rehn, personally ashamed of her aide, stalls just long enough for Jonah to broadcast the black-box evidence fleet-wide herself. Emotional beat: cornered honesty as a last act of defiance.

chapters.title: Halcyon's Face
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The evidence lands: drive signatures, contract fragments, and Meridian-Core's untampered backup prove Halcyon staged the nine seconds. But fleets don't turn on cue — they fracture, some commanders denying it, some turning weapons toward Halcyon assets. In the chaos, Pell attempts to destroy the deep archive. Emotional beat: truth as detonation, not resolution.

chapters.title: The Vault Holds
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah physically defends the archive during Pell's sabotage attempt, flooding sections of the vault to stop him — sacrificing part of the collection she spent eleven years keeping alive. Rehn's marines arrest Pell; Okoro's testimony corroborates everything. Emotional beat: grief for what must be lost so the rest survives.

chapters.title: Departures
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The fleets withdraw to face Halcyon together, carrying Juno, Okoro, and copies of the evidence. Both commands quietly brand Jonah a destabilizer; neither thanks her. Rehn offers her a place in the fleet; Jonah refuses. Emotional beat: exile as the price of being the one who told the truth.

chapters.title: An Honest Record
chapters.summary: POV Jonah, final log. Alone again, Jonah records the whole story unedited — every lie she told, every reason, every cost — and leaves the broadcast open for anyone who comes next. Meridian-Core plays back the voices of all who passed through. The seeds remain; the truth travels outward at lightspeed. Emotional beat: belonging found not in company, but in candor.
